content.text: Yes. Under Para 11 of the NBFC Credit Facilities Directions, 2025, the borrower must be given an explicit option to exit a digital loan during a cooling-off period by paying the principal and the proportionate APR, with no penalty. The NBFC sets the period in its credit policy, but it cannot be less than one day. The NBFC may keep a reasonable one-time processing fee if the borrower exits during that period, and any such fee must be disclosed upfront in the Key Facts Statement (KFS). Borrowers who stay past the cooling-off period remain subject to the pre-payment rules in the Responsible Business Conduct Directions.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: An NBFC must give every prospective borrower a Key Facts Statement in the standard Annex I format, including the APR computation sheet and the amortisation schedule, before the loan contract is executed. The KFS must carry a unique proposal number and stay valid for at least three working days, and the borrower must acknowledge having understood it.
findings.recommendation: Show the full KFS (APR, fees, repayment schedule, contingent charges) with a proposal number and validity period before the Accept step. Obtain an acknowledgement that the borrower has understood it. Do not rely on the post-acceptance confirmation screen or the emailed agreement.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: The KFS must disclose the interest rate, the processing fee and other charges, the APR (which includes all charges levied by the NBFC), and the contingent charges. Charges that cannot be determined before sanction may be shown as an upper ceiling. Revealing the processing fee and APR only after acceptance does not meet this.
findings.recommendation: Move the processing fee, other charges, APR and contingent charges (penal, foreclosure) onto the pre-acceptance KFS screen. The Accept screen should not show only the amount and instalment.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: For digital loans the borrower must get an explicit option to exit during a cooling-off period of at least one day by paying the principal and proportionate APR without penalty. Any reasonable one-time processing fee the NBFC retains on exit must be disclosed upfront in the KFS.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the journey offers an explicit cooling-off exit of at least one day. State the cooling-off terms and any retained processing fee in the KFS before acceptance, not only afterwards.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: The NBFC must convey the sanctioned amount and terms, including the annualised interest rate, in writing in a language the borrower understands and keep a record of the borrower's acceptance. It must also give a copy of the loan agreement and enclosures at sanction or disbursement. Digitally signed documents (KFS, sanction letter, terms) must flow automatically to the borrower's registered and verified email or SMS on execution of the contract.
findings.recommendation: Make sure the written terms, including the annualised rate, are conveyed in the borrower's language before acceptance, and that the acceptance is recorded. Email the digitally signed KFS, sanction letter and agreement to the verified address. Email delivery after acceptance does not replace pre-acceptance disclosure.

findings.obligation: The notice to the Data Principal must be understandable on its own and must itemise the personal data processed, the specified purposes and the services enabled, with links for withdrawing consent, exercising rights and complaining to the Board. A one-tap Accept on an amount-and-instalment screen does not show this.
findings.recommendation: Add a standalone consent notice before data is processed. It should list the personal data items and purposes in plain language and give the consent-withdrawal, rights and complaint links. Keep the loan-terms acceptance separate from the data consent.

11. Cooling-off period
(1) The borrower shall be given an explicit option to exit a digital loan by paying
the principal and the proportionate APR without any penalty during an initial
“cooling-off period”. The cooling off period shall be determined by the NBFC in
terms of their credit policy, subject to the period so determined not being less
than one day. For borrower continuing with the loan even after cooling-off
period, pre-payment shall continue to be allowed as per Reserve Bank of India
(Non-Banking Financial Companies- Responsible Business Conduct)
Directions, 2025.
(2) An NBFC may retain a reasonable one-time processing fee, if the customer
exits the loan during the cooling-off period. This, if applicable, shall be
disclosed to the customer upfront in KFS.

9. Disclosures to borrowers
(1) An NBFC shall provide a Key Fact Statement (KFS), as per instructions
contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non- Banking Financial Companies –
Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025.
(2) As regards penal charges, an NBFC shall be guided by Reserve Bank of India
(Non- Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct)
Directions, 2025.
(3) An NBFC shall ensure that digitally signed documents (on the letter head of
the NBFC) viz., KFS, summary of loan product, sanction letter, terms and
conditions, account statements, privacy policies of the NBFC / LSP with
respect to storage and usage of borrowers’ data, etc. shall automatically flow
to the borrower on the registered and verified email / SMS upon execution of
the loan contract / transactions.
Note: Digitally signed documents shall be in compliance with the provisions of
the Information Technology Act, 2000, as amended from time to time.
(4) An NBFC shall maintain a website of its own in public domain, which shall be
kept up to date, inter-alia, with the following details at a prominent single place
on the website for ease of accessibility:
(i) Details of all of its digital lending products and its DLAs.
(ii) Details of LSPs and the DLAs of the LSPs along with the details of the
activities for which they have been engaged for.
(iii) Particulars of NBFC’s customer care and internal grievance redressal
mechanism.
(iv) Link to the Reserve Bank’s Complaint Management System (CMS) and
Sachet Portal.
(v) Privacy policies and other details as required under extant guidelines of the
Reserve Bank.
(5) An NBFC shall ensure that DLAs / LSPs have links to the above website of the
NBFC.

29. The following instructions shall be applicable in case of all new retail and MSME
term loans sanctioned on or after October 1, 2024, including fresh loans to existing
customers, by an NBFC. Credit card receivables are exempted from the provisions
given below:
(1) An NBFC shall provide a KFS to all prospective borrowers to help them take an
informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format
given in the Annex I. The KFS shall be written in a language understood by such
borrowers. Contents of KFS shall be explained to the borrower and an
acknowledgement shall be obtained that they have understood the same.
(2) The KFS shall be provided with a unique proposal number and shall have a
validity period of at least three working days for loans having tenor of seven days
or more, and a validity period of one working day for loans having tenor of less than
seven days.
Explanation: Validity period refers to the period available to the borrower, after being
provided the KFS by the NBFC, to agree to the terms of the loan. The NBFC shall
be bound by the terms of the loan indicated in the KFS, if agreed to by the borrower
during the validity period.

(APR), and the amortisation schedule of the loan over the loan tenor. APR will
